source_caption:
🎬 Leave No Trace (2018)

Leave No Trace follows Will, a military veteran struggling with post-traumatic stress, and his teenage daughter Tom, who live a quiet, isolated life in the forests of Portland, Oregon. Far removed from modern society, the pair have built a peaceful existence surrounded by nature, relying on survival skills, simple routines, and their close relationship to get through each day. Although their unconventional lifestyle provides Will with a sense of safety, everything changes when authorities discover their hidden campsite and force them to return to society. Suddenly faced with unfamiliar expectations, social services, and the challenges of ordinary life, Will and Tom must adjust to a world they have spent years avoiding. While Tom begins discovering the possibilities of friendship, community, and independence, her father struggles with the emotional scars that make living among others increasingly difficult. As their needs and desires begin to diverge, the bond between father and daughter is tested in ways neither expected. Through quiet moments, emotional discoveries, and deeply human storytelling, the film explores the difficult choices people make when love and personal freedom pull them in different directions. Combining beautiful natural landscapes, powerful performances, and a moving portrayal of family relationships, Leave No Trace explores trauma, resilience, independence, belonging, sacrifice, and the complicated meaning of home.

🎭 Genre: Drama • Adventure

⭐ IMDb: 7.1/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 49m • PG

🎥 Director: Debra Granik

source_details.synopsis: Leave No Trace is a 2018 American drama film directed by Debra Granik. The film is written by Granik and Anne Rosellini, based on Peter Rock's 2009 novel My Abandonment, which is loosely based on a true story. The plot follows a military veteran father (Ben Foster) with post-traumatic stress disorder who lives in the forest with his young daughter (Thomasin McKenzie). Leave No Trace premiered at the 2018 Sundance Film Festival, and was theatrically released by Bleecker Street in the United States on June 29, 2018. It is the most reviewed film to hold a 100% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.
